exercises: a path item that is a $ref to another path item, which OAS 3.0 allows
note: The path item $ref is the one place in OAS 3.0 where a whole path item, rather than a component, is referenced. The referenced operation deliberately carries no operationId: once the reference resolves there are two operations with that id, and openapi-spec-validator rejects the document for a duplicate. That is a property of the construct, not of this fixture, and it means the browser cannot rely on an operationId being present to identify an operation reached this way.
doNotChangeFixture: Assertions marked pending describe correct behaviour the browser does not have yet. A failure on one of them is a backlog item, not a fixture defect. Do not edit this fixture or its expectations to match what the app currently does.

expected.assert: /titles renders with the same single GET operation as /books, including its limit parameter.
expected.why: The model walks each path item's keys and keeps only the HTTP method names, so a path item whose only key is $ref yields no operations and the path disappears.

expected.assert: The operation reached through /titles is presented under the path /titles, not under /books.
expected.why: Follows from the above: the path item is never resolved, so there is nothing to present.

expected.assert: Nothing crashes: a path item the browser cannot interpret must not take the rest of the document with it.
/books still renders its GET even though the operation has no operationId. An operation is identified by method plus path when no id is declared.
/books and /titles are separately addressable, even though they resolve to the same operation node with no operationId to tell them apart.
expected.why: Identity currently comes from the operationId or, failing that, method plus path. That fallback is correct here, but the path item is never resolved, so /titles produces no operation to address.
